business: Tirana events app: free discovery and one-tap join for community events (yoga, chess, book clubs, hikes); tickets for big commercial events sold in-app
why_not: I don't look for events, they find me through stories and friends reposting. I'm not going to open a separate app to browse a feed when my feed already shows me what my people are doing.
I never go looking for events, they find me through stories and friends' reposts. I would not open a separate app to browse a feed, and I have no money for concert tickets anyway.

I would download it because it is free and I do want to know what is happening in Tirana, but I would not actually join or pay for anything yet. Scrolling a feed is one thing; walking alone into a yoga class or a party full of strangers from an app is another, and by the end of the month I don't have 700 Lek spare anyway.

I already find things through my WhatsApp groups, and I go because I know who is going. A feed of events full of strangers does not fix the actual problem, which is that I am not showing up to a yoga class alone.

I would download it and join the free stuff for sure, the yoga and the hikes are exactly what I want instead of clubs. But buy a ticket? 700 Lek is my coffee money for a week, so the paid part of this app is not for me.

I would download it because the small events are free and that is all I ever join anyway, but buying a 700 Lek concert ticket through an app is not something I do — that is real money for me and I pay cash when I pay at all.
why_yes: I already go out most weeks and I am sick of finding out about things two days late on someone's story. If it is actually all in one place with real dates, I will use it, and I would buy one concert ticket through it if the price really is the same 700 Lek.
